summary: Mineral County, MT lookout on Little Joe Peak: cabin and platform tower from the 1920s, a 1969 tower moved to Williams Peak in 1977 and reported standing there in May 2026.

facts.design: 53-foot treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab (built 1969 at Little Joe)
facts.status_note: Tower and cab moved from Little Joe to Williams Peak in 1977; the structure stands there. No source describes what remains on the Little Joe summit.
facts.agency: Lolo National Forest for the Little Joe site (firelookout.com); Montana Fish, Wildlife and Parks administers the Williams Peak site (NHLR)

events.note: November 1921 newspaper item, quoted on Forest Lookouts, says towers were being built at Tamarack Point and Little Joe. firelookout.com dates the first log cabin and platform tower to the 1920s.
August 1927: lightning struck near the tower; the lookout could not be reached by telephone for two hours.
A 50-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab followed the early cabin and platform tower.
First of eight named lookout workers, 1955 to 1967 (firelookout.com 'Known lookout personnel' list).
Cab on display at the 1967 scout jamboree in Idaho before being placed on the tower.
53-foot treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab built at Little Joe.
Tower and cab moved to Williams Peak, replacing an older 30-foot 1934 tower with L-4 cab there.

corrections.why: The tower and cab were moved to Williams Peak in 1977 rather than destroyed, and a May 2026 report describes a lookout standing there. 'Relocated' describes the structure better than 'gone'.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com places Little Joe 4 miles southwest of St. Regis; the Forest Lookouts page quotes a survey station description of 5 miles southwest. The story reports both figures.

resolved_conflicts.field: agency for the Williams Peak site
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR says Montana Fish, Wildlife and Parks administers the site in Fish Creek State Park. firelookout.com's Williams Peak page lists Lolo National Forest but also says the lookout sits on state property. The 2026 report describes a Forest Service road (FS-7721). The story follows the NHLR administrator and the state-property note.

sources.title: Little Joe Mtn. Fire Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: Record status 'gone' is proposed as 'relocated': the tower and cab moved to Williams Peak in 1977 and the May 2026 report describes a lookout there. The Little Joe summit itself has no source describing what, if anything, remains, and no source gives visiting or access rules for either site; access is omitted from facts. Staffing 'unstaffed' comes from the Williams Peak page, not from Little Joe; the Little Joe personnel list ends in 1967. Not used in the story: firelookout.com gives Little Joe elevation 5398 ft, while mineralcounty.info (Little Joe Lookout Station) gives 5174 ft. The Scout jamboree is spelled Farragut (NHLR) and Farrugut (firelookout.com). The NHLR registration (March 20, 2016, US 1119, MT 63) belongs to the Williams Peak lookout, so it is left out of Little Joe's events. Search budget: one websearch.py query and six page reads for this tower.
